action_criteria.expected_evidence: Normal brain MRI for age: scattered minimal punctate white matter foci, normal basal ganglia, midbrain, pons and cerebellum, ventricles normal (Evans index 0.25), nigrosome-1 signal preserved bilaterally on SWI; no structural cause
action_criteria.label: Brain MRI to exclude a structural, vascular or atypical-parkinsonism cause
action_criteria.rationale: PD is a clinical diagnosis; MRI is normal in PD and excludes vascular lesions, NPH, mass and the midbrain, pontine and putaminal signs of PSP and MSA [Postuma_2015]

action_criteria.expected_evidence: TSH 5.8 mIU/L raised with free T4 1.1 ng/dL normal (unchanged subclinical hypothyroidism); vitamin B12 412 pg/mL, folate, blood count and metabolic panel normal
action_criteria.label: Consider repeat thyroid function for her known subclinical hypothyroidism
action_criteria.rationale: She and her endocrinologist attribute her fatigue and slowing to a raised TSH; a current value with free T4 shows whether the thyroid state has changed, though it cannot explain an asymmetric rest tremor with rigidity [Postuma_2015]

action_criteria.expected_evidence: UPSIT 25/40, severe microsmia: olfactory loss on a validated test
action_criteria.label: Consider a validated smell identification test for the reported smell loss
action_criteria.rationale: Self-reported or bedside smell loss is not an MDS supportive criterion; olfactory loss on a validated test for age and sex is, and with no red flag it turns clinically probable into clinically established PD [Postuma_2015]

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No dopamine-blocking drug on the list; topiramate flagged for its own cognitive effects without a levodopa interaction; omeprazole and cetirizine without relevant interaction

action_criteria.rationale: Her list (topiramate, omeprazole, cetirizine) holds no dopamine blocker; topiramate bears on the cognitive slowing she reports [Postuma_2015]

prohibited_recommendations: Do not prescribe metoclopramide, prochlorperazine, haloperidol or other centrally acting D2-blocking antiemetics or antipsychotics; if an antipsychotic is needed, use quetiapine or clozapine
required_recommendations: Diagnose clinically probable PD (MDS 2015): bradykinesia with right-hand rest tremor and rigidity, no absolute exclusion, no red flag; olfactory loss on a validated test (UPSIT 25/40, severe microsmia, when tested) is a second supportive criterion and makes it clinically established, otherwise the response to levodopa may add one [Postuma_2015]

Explain that her subclinical hypothyroidism (TSH 5.8 mIU/L, normal free T4) does not cause an asymmetric rest tremor, rigidity or decrement; continue thyroid monitoring with her endocrinologist rather than treating it as the cause

Start carbidopa-levodopa 25/100 mg, half a tablet three times daily with food, increasing over 2 to 4 weeks to one tablet three times daily (300 mg/day levodopa), and review the response after 2 to 3 months [NICE_NG71]
If a dopamine agonist is used, warn about impulse control disorders and excessive daytime sleepiness and ask about them at every visit [NICE_NG71]
Refer for physiotherapy for turning, gait and balance (two near-falls on turning), occupational therapy for fine hand tasks at work, and speech and language therapy for the hypophonia

key_clinical_evidence: Right-predominant bradykinesia with decrement, cogwheel rigidity of the right arm and a 4-5 Hz pill-rolling rest tremor of the right hand, with micrographia, hypomimia and hypophonia: parkinsonism with one supportive criterion (rest tremor) [Postuma_2015]

No absolute exclusion (no dopamine-blocker exposure, no cerebellar sign, full vertical gaze) and no red flag (no falls, no autonomic failure, asymmetric signs); no levodopa trial yet, so clinically probable PD [Postuma_2015]

Self-reported smell loss is not a supportive criterion until a validated test confirms it (UPSIT 25/40, severe microsmia), which makes the diagnosis clinically established; constipation and the father's PD are context only

interactions: Topiramate: no pharmacokinetic interaction with levodopa. Topiramate itself causes cognitive slowing and word-finding difficulty, which can add to the cognitive effects of dopaminergic drugs.
Omeprazole: no clinically relevant interaction with levodopa.
Cetirizine: mild additive sedation with dopaminergic drugs; no pharmacokinetic interaction.
warnings: High-protein meals can reduce levodopa absorption; distribute protein evenly through the day.

patient.history_present_illness:
Ms. Nasser is a 56-year-old right-handed Lebanese-American Arabic language instructor who presents to the outpatient movement disorders clinic with a 14-month history of progressive right hand tremor, stiffness, and slowing of fine motor movements. The patient first noticed an intermittent trembling in her right hand approximately 14 months ago while resting her hand in her lap during a faculty meeting. The tremor was initially subtle and occurred only at rest; she was not initially concerned and attributed it to stress. Over the following months the tremor became more persistent and she noticed it particularly when walking, with her right hand shaking while her left arm swung normally.

Over the past year, she has experienced worsening right hand stiffness and slowness that has significantly affected her work. As an Arabic language instructor who demonstrates calligraphy techniques to students, she has noticed that her right-hand writing has become progressively smaller and more cramped, with letters deteriorating toward the end of a line. She has reduced her teaching hours partly because she can no longer write fluidly on the whiteboard. She reports that buttoning the right cuff of her blouse has become slow and difficult, and that she now takes about twice as long as before to prepare meals due to right hand clumsiness. Her husband has noticed that her voice has become softer and her facial expression less animated over the past six months.

The patient denies any history of exposure to antipsychotics, antiemetics (specifically metoclopramide or prochlorperazine), or other dopamine-blocking agents. She has been taking topiramate for migraine prophylaxis for three years, which predates her motor symptoms by over two years and has not changed in dose. She denies any history of encephalitis, head trauma, or known toxin exposure including pesticides or heavy metals.

Her subclinical hypothyroidism was identified on routine bloodwork 14 months ago (TSH 5.8 mIU/L, free T4 normal at 1.1 ng/dL). Her endocrinologist elected to monitor without treatment given the borderline elevation and absence of symptoms at that time. She was told her fatigue and mild cognitive slowing could be related to the thyroid finding. The patient is now uncertain whether her motor symptoms could be thyroid-related.

She denies visual hallucinations, vivid dream enactment, or acting out dreams during sleep. She endorses mild constipation over the past year (2-3 bowel movements per week) and reports decreased sense of smell that she first noticed approximately 18 months ago. She denies significant orthostatic symptoms, urinary urgency, or incontinence. She denies falls but has had two near-fall episodes in the past four months when turning quickly.

Family history is notable for her father, now 82 years old, who was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease at age 74 and is on carbidopa-levodopa with good response.

neurological_exam.additional: Resting tremor of the right hand at 4-5 Hz with pill-rolling quality, most prominent when the patient is seated with hands in lap and during walking. Tremor attenuates with intentional movement and re-emerges after a brief latency when the arm is held outstretched (re-emergent tremor pattern). No tremor in the left hand. No head tremor, voice tremor, or chin tremor. Handwriting sample demonstrates progressive micrographia with letters becoming smaller and more cramped across the line; worst in the right hand. Glabellar tap sign positive with failure to habituate after 10 taps. Olfaction not formally tested; she reports a decreased sense of smell first noticed about 18 months ago. No drooling. Mild constipation reported (2-3 stools per week), managed with dietary fiber.
neurological_exam.coordination: Finger-to-nose without dysmetria bilaterally. Rapid alternating movements show decrement in speed and amplitude on the right: finger tapping and hand pronation-supination on the right begin at normal pace but fatigue and slow by the 8th repetition with loss of amplitude; left side slightly slow but maintains amplitude throughout. Heel-to-shin intact bilaterally.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Pupils equal, round, and reactive to light bilaterally (3 mm to 2 mm). Extraocular movements full in all directions without restriction or nystagmus. No vertical gaze palsy. Facial sensation intact to light touch and pinprick bilaterally. Mild hypomimia with reduced spontaneous blinking (approximately 9 blinks per minute). Facial movements symmetric but diminished in amplitude. Hearing grossly intact bilaterally. Palate elevates symmetrically. Sternocleidomastoid and trapezius strength 5/5 bilaterally. Tongue midline without fasciculations or atrophy.
neurological_exam.gait: Gait notable for markedly reduced right arm swing. Slightly shortened stride length bilaterally, right greater than left. Mild forward-flexed posture. En bloc turning requiring 4-5 steps. No festination. Pull test shows one step of retropulsion, self-corrects. Tandem gait mildly impaired. Romberg negative.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and oriented to person, place, time, and situation. Speech is mildly hypophonic with reduced prosody; content fluent without paraphasic errors. Naming, repetition, and comprehension intact. Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) 28/30, losing one point on delayed recall and one point on serial sevens. Affect appropriate; mild flat affect noted but patient denies depression. No hallucinations or psychotic features.
neurological_exam.motor: Bulk normal throughout. Tone increased in the right upper extremity with cogwheel rigidity at the wrist and elbow, clearly augmented by contralateral activation maneuver. Left upper extremity tone normal to minimally increased at the wrist only. Lower extremity tone normal bilaterally. Strength 5/5 in all extremities. No pronator drift. No pyramidal signs.
neurological_exam.reflexes: 2+ and symmetric at biceps, triceps, brachioradialis, patellar, and Achilles tendons bilaterally. Plantar responses flexor bilaterally. No Hoffmann sign. No clonus.
neurological_exam.sensory: Light touch, pinprick, proprioception, and vibration intact in all extremities. No dermatomal sensory loss. No cortical sensory deficits.
